breaks.title: After a merge, the Rig re-sends the other save's changes to the team canvas as its own new edit, undoing any canvas edit made since that save. Reopening the Rig then copies the stale canvas into the draft.
breaks.scenario: flush() calls publishRef(now.project, merged) after every merged save. That is diffForTeam over the fields the OTHER save changed, sent as a fresh PATCH with the server's current stamp. saveDraft's own diff had already put those fields on the canvas, so the re-send only matters when the canvas has moved on since, and then it reverts that newer edit. (a) Rig A has been open since before window B retitled Opening to 'Title from window B'. A teammate then retitles it on the canvas to 'Teammate title'. A edits only Second's note, gets a 409 and merges. The canvas now reads 'Title from window B' and the teammate's later rename is gone. (b) Same user: B renames Opening to 'B first rename', and A merges it in. A's post-merge PATCH is slow, and B renames again to 'B second rename', which its save puts on the canvas. A's PATCH then lands and the canvas reads 'B first rename'. Reloading the Rig copies the canvas into the draft and saves it, so the draft ends at 'B first rename' too. B's latest rename is lost from both, and every window says Saved. (c) B deletes Second, and the canvas removes it. A teammate edits Second's prompt on the canvas, which by design brings it back. A (stale, never touched Second) merges and publishes removeNodes [n2]. Second is taken off the canvas again (canvas.removedIds=['n2'], the teammate's text is no longer live), and the teammate's next join drops it from their draft. origin/main reloaded on a conflict and never published.

breaks.title: Coming back to a project whose background save is still in flight: that save lands later and puts the older note back over the note typed after coming back
breaks.scenario: Rig on A. The server returns 503, the note 'Note typed before leaving' does not save, and the person switches to B, so A's draft is parked and saved in the background. One parked attempt hangs on a slow connection. The person switches back to A: back.stop=true is set and back.draft becomes the Rig's draft, but the attempt already out keeps going (stop is only checked between attempts, and the parked write and the Rig share one writer). The Rig saves the parked draft (PUT base=1 → rev 2), then the person types 'Note typed after coming back' (PUT base=2 → rev 3). The hung parked PUT (base=1) now arrives and gets a 409. writeMergedDraft reads rev 3 and runs mergeDraft(parkBase, parkedMine, latest). Both sides changed the note, so mine (the parked 'before leaving') wins, and it PUTs base=3. Server note: 'Note typed before leaving'. The Rig shows 'Note typed after coming back' and 'Saved'. The Rig's next merge shows the older note, so the newer edit is silently lost. PUT log: 503×9 (base=1), held base=1, pass base=1, pass base=2 (after), released base=1 → 409, pass base=3 (before).

breaks.title: Generate with an unsaved edit now merges and goes on, but renders from the shot and node it read before the merge: a take paid at the old settings and prompt, while the Rig shows and saves the merged shot
breaks.spec: tests/zz-break-canvas-undo-r2-4-workbench.spec.ts (failed on 2 runs; the quote is refused by route.fulfill after its body is recorded, so nothing is billed)
breaks.scenario: Opening has 'Original prompt: a fox on the ice.' at 5 s. Another window rewrites it to 'Prompt from window B: the harbour at night.' at 10 s. The Rig types a direction note and presses Generate take before the note saves. generate() captures shot/node/refs at line 418. flush() gets a 409, merges and returns true (origin/main refused here with 'Save your latest work before generating'). shotRequestInput(current, node, shot, …) then builds the request from the pre-merge node and shot. The body POSTed to /api/generate/quote is prompt 'Original prompt: a fox on the ice.\n\nDirector's notes: Hold on the fox.', duration 5. After the merge, the Inspector shows B's prompt and '10s', and the saved draft has text=B's prompt and durationS=10. The price shown was also for the stale 5 s settings, so the dispatch gate passes and a real render would bill a take that matches neither the screen nor the saved shot.

breaks.title: ⌘Z on project B can never reach B's own delete while a Rig undo for project A sits above it on the shared undo stack
breaks.scenario: On B, delete 'Bravo second' (by mistake). Switch to A and delete 'Alpha second'. Back on B, press ⌘Z (twice). Each press pops A's entry. The new home check (RigProvider:589) throws 'Open Alpha … to bring Alpha second back.', and the entry is pushed back on top (state.tsx:196), so B's older entry is never reached. B's draft stays ['b1']. The only way back is to undo A's intended delete first. No data is lost (the workaround exists), but in the Suites shell, where Delete has no confirmation, ⌘Z is the only way back for a deleted shot.

breaks.title: (Pre-existing on origin/main, not introduced by this diff) A canvas edit to project A that failed to send is later sent to project B's canvas, and B's Rig then copies A's shot into B's draft
breaks.scenario: Rig on A, and the team-canvas PATCH returns 503. Edit a-n1's note: the canvas PATCH (productionId A) fails and stays pending, with a retry every 5 s. Switch to B. The pending patch is merged into B's join patch, and send() reads pid = joined.current at send time (now B). PATCH log: A, A, A, then B with upsertNodes [a-n1, b-n1]. B's canvas holds a-n1. Reopening B's Rig copies it into B's draft and saves it, and B's draft becomes [a-n1, b-n1]. The pending patch is not keyed by the production it was made for. This code predates the branch, but it sits squarely in the switch-mid-save / canvas-consistency path the branch relies on.

breaks.title: A 503 on a draft PUT counts as an uncertain write, so each save attempt sends 4 PUTs and 3 check-writes back to back, with no pause between them
breaks.spec: observed in the PUT log of tests/zz-break-canvas-undo-r2-2-workbench.spec.ts (timestamped probe: 4 PUTs within 40 ms, then 5 within 100 ms)
breaks.scenario: While the server answers 503, each writeMergedDraft call runs PUT → 503 (uncertain) → check-write (not landed) → merge → PUT, up to MERGE_TRIES+1 times back to back. The Rig flush and a parked save each do this at the same time. It is bounded, and backoff only applies between calls, but against an overloaded server this multiplies load. Not a correctness break.

Team canvas after a merge: server-side saveDraft diff (field-level, onlyIfShared) plus client publish(now→merged). The client re-publish is redundant and reverts newer canvas edits (break 1: teammate rename, same-user later rename then draft loss via join, teammate-restored shot re-removed)
